transfers.source_mechanism: adaptive network formation through feedback between exploration and resource utilization
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: adaptive traffic signal timing through feedback between local exploration and flow optimization
transfers.required_translation: replace protoplasmic streaming with vehicle movement, resource locations with traffic demand, network reinforcement with signal timing adjustments, and path pruning with phase optimization
transfers.expected_effect: distributed optimization of traffic signal timing that adapts to real-time conditions without central coordination
boundary_conditions: local measurement constraints (vehicle count and queue length only)
failure_conditions: environmental barriers (unpredictable events exceeding adaptation capacity)
transfers.testable_prediction: When implementing this distributed system, the average intersection delay should decrease by at least 15% compared to the current semi-optimized system during normal conditions, and the system should adapt to incidents within 10 minutes (measured from incident occurrence to when delay returns to within 5% of pre-incident levels)
